subject: Request: Temporary priority shift + runbook for Helios enterprise pilot (GPU pool)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@helioslabs.ai>, ops@helioslabs.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary priority shift + runbook for Helios enterprise pilot (GPU pool)

Team —

Quick context: Helios Labs (enterprise pilot) ramped up their nightly fine-tuning runs last week and caused recurring contention in the east-us-gpu-pool between 02:00–06:00 UTC. Their pilot is strategic (potential Dedicated contract) and they’re asking for a short-term operational guarantee while we finalize a dedicated carve-out.

Ask: Approve a temporary priority shift (soft-reservation) for Helios to get an extra priority band during their critical nightly window for 7 calendar days starting 2027-05-05. This would be an autoscaling-policy exception + routing priority tweak (not a long-term Dedicated commit).

Key constraints / acceptance criteria:
- Max burst capacity: up to 4x their baseline slot usage but capped at 60 GPU-hours/day aggregate.
- No SLA changes for other enterprise customers — traffic should gracefully degrade to normal priority outside the window.
- Audit: all request routing and cost delta tracked; finance wants a quick estimate before approval.

I’ve drafted a short runbook and a capacity plan (attached) that covers: request gating, escalation path, SRE throttles, rollback steps, and billing note. Please review availability and safety concerns. Specific asks:
1) Ben — confirm whether the runtime supports a temporary priority band and estimate ops effort to enable/disable for 7 days.
2) Marissa — provide ballpark cost delta and whether we should issue a usage credit vs invoice.
3) Hannah — any product-side flags we should check (quota gating, routing policies) and whether the console needs a visible flag for the customer during the window.

If we can get a go/no-go by EOD 2027-05-03, I’ll send Helios the operational plan and proposed start date.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: helios_capacity_plan.xlsx)
(attachment: temp_priority_runbook_v1.md)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary priority shift + runbook for Helios enterprise pilot (GPU pool)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear plan and attachments. I skimmed the capacity plan; a few quick notes on cost:
- Based on their current baseline and the 4x burst cap, rough incremental compute cost (GPU-hours) is ~ $1,800/day before discounts.
- If we do a short-term operational credit to keep the pilot moving, finance recommends a capped credit (e.g., 50% of the incremental compute for the 7 days) rather than absorbing full cost.
- We should include a single-line item in the pilot MOU stating the credit and dates. I can draft the MOU addendum if you want.

Question for Ben: can we meter the extra priority separately so finance can clearly attribute usage and credit it? If not, tracking will be noisy.

Happy to draft the customer-facing note once ops confirms feasibility.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary priority shift + runbook for Helios enterprise pilot (GPU pool)

Vanessa / team —

We can implement a temporary priority band in the routing layer without code changes; it’s a policy config change plus a small SRE chore to apply and monitor. Implementation notes:
- Steps: create priority label `pilot:helios_temp` -> map to higher queue weight during 02:00–06:00 UTC -> attach throttles to cap at the 60 GPU-hours/day aggregate.
- Metering: we can tag requests with `pilot_id` and produce a daily usage export. That will let finance reconcile and apply the credit cleanly.
- Risk: If other high-priority customers spike unexpectedly during that window, we’ll see latency impact. I recommend we add an automated rollback trigger: if p95 latency on production routes increases > 15% vs baseline for 10m, auto-disable the band and page SRE.
- Ops effort: ~3 engineer-hours to configure, test in staging, and schedule the window. Monitoring dashboards: I’ll add a temporary panel and alert.

I reviewed the runbook (temp_priority_runbook_v1.md). A couple of additions I’ll make before we flip:
- Add a step to pre-warm KV cache for Helios large-model runs at their window start.
- Add explicit steps for pausing burst if storage I/O becomes the bottleneck rather than GPU.

If we align on the credit approach Marissa suggested, we good from an infra standpoint. 

—Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
(see: JIRA INFRA-7842)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@helioslabs.ai>, ops@helioslabs.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary priority shift + runbook for Helios enterprise pilot (GPU pool)

Thanks all — consensus looks positive. Quick summary and next steps (action owners):

1) Infra (Ben): spin up the `pilot:helios_temp` band, add the throttle/rollback triggers, and create the daily usage export. ETA: 2027-05-04 EOD for staging test. (JIRA INFRA-7842)
2) Sales (Marissa): draft an MOU addendum with the 7-day credit proposal (50% of incremental compute). Send to Vanessa for review. ETA: 2027-05-03 EOD.
3) Product (Hannah): confirm there are no quota gating side-effects and add a UI flag suggestion for visibility during the window. Quick check by 2027-05-04 morning.
4) Ops/Customer: I’ll send Helios the operational plan and proposed start date 2027-05-05 02:00 UTC once we have infra staging verification.

If staging proves flaky, we’ll push by 24–48 hours. I’ll attach the finalized runbook after Ben’s small edits.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: temp_priority_runbook_v1.md - will update post infra edits)
